body_text:
Contour Integration and the Estimation Lemma.

Let $\gamma: [a, b] \to U$ be a piecewise smooth path and let $f: U \to \mathbb{C}$ be continuous.
The *contour integral* of $f$ along $\gamma$ is defined by:
$$ \int_\gamma f(z)\,dz = \int_a^b f(\gamma(t)) \gamma'(t)\,dt, $$
where the integral on the right-hand side is evaluated as the sum of ordinary Riemann integrals
of its real and imaginary parts. The integral is invariant under orientation-preserving
reparameterizations, while reversing orientation replaces $\gamma$ by $-\gamma$ and flips the sign:
$\int_{-\gamma} f(z)\,dz = -\int_\gamma f(z)\,dz$.

**The $ML$-Inequality (Estimation Lemma)**: If $|f(z)| \le M$ for all $z$ on the trace of $\gamma$,
and $L(\gamma) = \int_a^b |\gamma'(t)|\,dt$ denotes the arc length of $\gamma$, then:
$$ \left| \int_\gamma f(z)\,dz \right| \le \int_a^b |f(\gamma(t))| |\gamma'(t)|\,dt \le M \cdot L(\gamma). $$
This elementary bound is the foundational tool for establishing convergence of contour integrals
along expanding circular arcs and vanishing contours.
